item.title: Tilney St Lawrence man charged following King’s Lynn retail park incident
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Tilney St Lawrence man charged following King’s Lynn retail park incident
A 24-year-old man from Tilney St Lawrence has been charged with drink-driving following reports of anti-social driving at the Hardwick Retail Park in King’s Lynn. Police were called to the site last Friday evening after receiving reports of vehicles drifting and performing handbrake turns.
Officers stopped a BMW at the scene, which was subsequently seized. The driver, Tom Perry of St John’s Road, was arrested and later charged with drink-driving. He has been bailed to appear at Lynn Magistrates Court on September 24. Norfolk Police have reminded the public that they have powers to seize vehicles involved in anti-social behaviour.

item.title: Wisbech veteran calls for review of state pension advice for ex-service personnel
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech veteran calls for review of state pension advice for ex-service personnel
A Wisbech veteran is calling on the government to review how state pensions are managed for former service personnel. Mo Stewart, a former medical technician, claims she was incorrectly told in 2019 that she had to choose between her war pension and her state pension.
The Department for Work and Pensions has apologised for the error and confirmed that its Complaint Resolution Team is investigating the matter urgently. Ms Stewart is now urging authorities to contact thousands of disabled war pensioners to ensure they are receiving their full entitlements. She is also calling for support for the families of deceased veterans who may have been misdirected regarding their pension claims in the past.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/veteran-calls-for-review-after-claiming-ex-service-personnel-9481883/

item.title: Man arrested following assault in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Man arrested following assault in King’s Lynn
A man in his 20s has been arrested following an assault on Norfolk Street in King’s Lynn. Police were called to the scene shortly before 1am on Sunday morning after reports that a woman working at a business premises had been headbutted. The victim sustained a broken nose and a broken eye socket during the incident.
Officers are now appealing for any witnesses who have not yet come forward to get in touch. Anyone with information should contact Norfolk Police on 101, quoting crime reference 36/66935/26. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to the charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

item.title: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
A series of cases were heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court last Thursday. Among those sentenced, 49-year-old Antonio Vaz was fined for stalking after installing a tracking device in a partner’s handbag.
In other matters, 47-year-old Clare Collins received a suspended prison sentence and a three-year driving ban for drink-driving, while 27-year-old Kane Curtis was disqualified for 12 months for a similar offence. Additionally, Kwok Wai Ho was handed 170 hours of unpaid work for driving while disqualified, and Ellie Marriott was fined for shoplifting and assault. Finally, an arrest warrant was issued for 21-year-old Harry Burley after he failed to appear at court for sentencing regarding a burglary charge.

item.title: New horror film Leviticus gains festival attention
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New horror film Leviticus gains festival attention
A new horror film titled Leviticus is gaining attention on the international film festival circuit. Directed by Adrian Chiarella, the movie follows two young men, played by Joe Bird and Stacy Clausen, living in a conservative Australian community. Their secret relationship takes a terrifying turn when a religious ritual releases a mysterious entity that can take the form of the person its victim desires most.
The film, which premiered at Sundance, has been praised for its suspenseful atmosphere and lead performances. While critics have noted similarities to the film It Follows, the production is being highlighted for its visual style and emotional narrative.
